profile.headline: Software Engineer en Change Healthcare
profile.summary:
Experience developing Java Web applications focused to back­end components. Recent experience has been to work with Java language and Play Framework to create ​web services based on REST​ and Gradle scripts for project automation and continuous delivery.
I enjoy to do challenge ­things with software development and my passion is to solve problems. I enjoy discovering new things and implement them.
I started my personal blog (www.albevia.com) where I share my knowledge with the last discoverings based on software development.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Maintenance, support, and new developments for a huge software system.
Java, PL/SQL, Gradle, GitLab, Confluence, Oracle, C# are some of the tools that we are using.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Customer: Equator (Plano Texas)
Use of RedHat Fuse and its different components such as ActiveMQ, Fabriq 8,
Apache Karaf, OSGi, Camel, and so on. And prepare the proof of concepts to the team about these tools. The goal was to prepare the current legacy applications to create software highly scalable and maintainable.


Customer: Navistar (Lisle, USA)

Technical support for Legacy Java Applications based on MQ and Enterprise Integration Hub.
Creating proofs of concepts to upgrade them and creating software tools to monitor the servers indicators.
Continuous integration to improve the quality of software.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
IBM has an area focused to the security of different types of equipment connected to the IBM network; the team was integrated with people with background on network security writing scripts using Perl. I helped to change their area implementing best practices and continuous integration. The team was formed with 14 members and I learn Perl to understand the legacy code. We started to create a web application named IEM (IBM Endpoint Management) and it was finished in 
March of this year. This web application exploit the API of Tivoli Endpoint Management and it is used to have the control of all the resources of all IBM servers. Examples of tasks that STG Security Area could do with this new web application are: monitor that each server compliance with the IBM policies, monitor that each server has the latest software update installed, etcetera. The web application was constructed using Java and Spring framework, and this application was connected to the Tivoli Endpoint Manager through its API based on RESTful services.
